title: Cheapest gift on the registry
author: Storytime
hook: I bought the cheapest gift on my best friend's wedding registry. She called me out for it in front of everyone.
story: My best friend Hannah got married in September. Her registry was all expensive stuff. Fancy mixers, designer towels, a two thousand dollar couch. I bought the cheapest thing on the list. A twenty dollar wooden spoon set. At the reception, Hannah did a gift speech. She thanked every guest by name and what they gave. When she got to me, she held up the spoons and said, and thank you to my maid of honor, for these, I guess. Everyone laughed. I smiled and said nothing. Here's what she didn't know. Six months earlier, Hannah told me she'd always dreamed of the honeymoon suite at the hotel in Santorini, but they couldn't afford it. So I called the hotel. I paid for the upgrade myself. Fourteen hundred dollars. I asked them to keep it anonymous, and just say it was a gift from someone who loves her. Last week, she got back from Santorini. She posted the suite everywhere. Her caption said, still don't know who did this, but thank you, whoever you are. Then she texted me, sorry about the spoons joke, it was just for fun. Should I tell her?
caption: the spoons were NOT the gift 🥄 #storytime
sound: a sweet, slightly bittersweet acoustic guitar at very low volume
why: Wedding registry drama is a proven viral genre, the cheap gift sets up the misunderstanding, the anonymous upgrade is the twist, and should I tell her splits the comments.

title: Boss denied my PTO for the wedding
author: Storytime
hook: My boss denied my day off for my sister's wedding. Then I saw his own calendar.
story: My little sister is getting married this Saturday. I requested the day off back in June. Five months notice. Last Monday, my boss, Richard, denied it. He said Saturdays are all hands, no exceptions, and if I didn't show up, I shouldn't come back Monday. I was furious. I went to HR, and while I was waiting, I saw Richard's shared calendar on the screen. He had blocked off this Saturday. All day. Out of office. Family wedding. I almost laughed. I told the HR lady, so the rule is no exceptions, except for him? She looked confused and pulled up the details. The wedding Richard is going to is at the Lakeside Inn. At four o'clock. My sister's wedding is at the Lakeside Inn. At four o'clock. My sister is marrying a guy named Kevin. Kevin's last name is Holt. Richard's last name is Holt. My boss is my sister's future father-in-law. And he has no idea I'm the bride's brother. HR approved my day off on the spot. I haven't told Richard. I'm giving a speech on Saturday, right after his. Part two?
caption: no exceptions. except his son's wedding 💼 #storytime
sound: a sneaky, building comedic beat at very low volume
why: PTO denied for a family wedding is a top workplace rage topic, the matching last names are the planted clue, and the speech after his speech is a great part two setup.

title: Anonymous notes on my car at the gym
author: Storytime
hook: Every morning at the gym, someone left an anonymous note on my car. I finally found out who.
story: This year, I decided to get healthy. I started going to the gym at six every morning. I was the slowest person on every machine. Then one morning, there was a sticky note on my windshield. It said, you're doing great, keep going. The next day, another one. I see you. Don't stop. For three months, every single morning, a new note. I lost thirty pounds. Last week, I came out early, and saw someone placing the note. It was Mr. Daniels. The old man who always walks on the treadmill next to mine. He looked embarrassed. Then he told me why. His daughter used to come to this gym. She quit because people laughed at her. She never came back. She stopped going out at all. He said he couldn't help her back then. But he could help me. I asked if I could meet her. He said she'd like that. So this Saturday, she's coming to the gym. With me. I'm more nervous than I was on my first day. Any advice?
caption: the notes were from him the whole time 💛 #storytime
sound: an uplifting, gentle piano that slowly builds at very low volume
why: Gym and fitness journeys reach a huge audience, the daily notes create mystery, the reveal is heartwarming, and asking for advice pulls supportive comments.
